# dsh-battery-level-indicator
**English** · 简体中文

Shows the **host computer's** battery in the composer dock — the row directly below the message
comp
oser — in the DeepSeek Harness Web UI.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- Percentage remaining, with a battery glyph whose fill follows the level.
- Charging state: `Chargi

ng`, `Finishing charge`, `Fully charged`, `Plugged in`, or `On battery`.
- While running on battery

it also shows the estimated time left.
- Below 20% on battery the readout switches to the error colo

r.
- Text comes from the Client locale service (`en`, `zh`), so it follows the app language.

Open the same Web UI on a phone or tablet and it still reports the computer's battery, because the
r
eading is taken on the Host — see below.
## Why the Host reads the battery

The value must describe the computer running Harness, not the device showing the page. The browser
B

attery Status API reports the *viewing* device, so a phone that opens the same Web UI would show
its
own charge. Version 1.1.0 therefore moved the reading to the Host:

1. `index.js` samples the machine battery, caches the result for 4 s, and serves it as JSON at
`GET

/battery-indicator/state`. The route applies Connection's Host/Origin and
browser-authentication che

cks before answering.
2. `client.js` polls that route (20 s, plus `visibilitychange` and `focus`), t

ries the
document-relative URL before the origin-root URL so a mounted deployment still resolves, an

d
keeps the last good reading through a transient failure.

The Client never calls `navigator.getBattery()`; on a phone that would report the phone. When the
Ho
st has no battery, or the sample cannot be parsed, the row says so instead of guessing.
## Platforms
| Platform | Source | Notes |

| macOS | `/usr/bin/pmset -g batt` via `ctx.subprocess` | Charge state and time remaining |
| Linux
| `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT*/` | `capacity`, `status`, and a countdown from `energy_now`/`power_n

ow` |
| Windows | — | Reports `unsupported-platform`; the row says the battery is unavailable |
Both sample paths return the same JSON shape, so the Client does not know which platform it is on:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`state` is one of `charging`, `finishing`, `charged`, `discharging`, `idle`, `unknown` — a small
clo
sed vocabulary the Client translates, so a new platform only has to map onto it.
## Files
| File | Role |

| `package.json` | Bundle manifest: patch, `dsh.client`, exports, `files` |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | I

nserts the `battery-indicator` row |
| `index.js` | Host half: samples `pmset` or sysfs, serves `/ba

ttery-indicator/state` |
| `parse.js` | Pure parsers for both platforms, so the shapes can be tested

anywhere |
| `client.js` | Slot registration in `conversation.composer.dock` and the readout compon

ent |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` | Plugin Manager / Settings title and description |
| `ic
on.svg` | Plugin icon |
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The parsers are pure, so the suite runs on any machine — including CI boxes with no battery.
## Changelog

- **1.2.0** — Linux support through sysfs; parsers extracted to `parse.js` with a test suite;
fixed

`discharging` being classified as `charging` (the check for `charging` ran before
`discharging`, and

the latter contains the former).
- **1.1.0** — Moved the reading to the Host so every device shows

the computer's battery.
- **1.0.0** — First version, using the browser Battery Status API.
